analysis.one_liner: Lets the Postal Service offer small-dollar loans, savings accounts, and prepaid cards.
analysis.headline: Postal banking bill never got a hearing or vote after being referred to the House Oversight Committee.
analysis.plain_summary: Would expand USPS authority to offer basic financial services like small-dollar loans, checking and savings accounts, international money transfers, and a 'Postal Card'.
analysis.who_benefits: Unbanked and underbanked Americans lacking access to traditional banking, postal workers, and people facing high costs from check-cashing stores and payday lenders.

how_it_helps.text: Provides access to basic banking through postal infrastructure, especially for low-income Americans in banking deserts.
Allows small-dollar loans through USPS, offering a cheaper alternative to payday lenders charging high interest rates.
Would help reverse decline in postal revenue and create new revenue streams for USPS.

analysis.who_pays: Traditional banks, payday lenders, and check-cashing businesses that currently serve these customers.

drawbacks.text: USPS already faced significant financial losses; adding financial services might compound existing operational challenges.
The bill was only referred to committee, never debated or voted on.

analysis.benefit_vs_cost: The bill would have provided an important public alternative for financial services to underserved communities, though concerns about USPS capacity and financial position are legitimate.

outcome.mechanism: The bill was referred to the House Oversight and Government Reform Committee but never received a hearing or floor vote before Congress ended.

narrative.text: Introduced February 1, 2016 and referred to the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform the same day.
No further action was taken; the bill died in committee.

outcome.who_came_out_ahead: Traditional banks and payday lenders retained their market position without a public postal banking alternative competing with them.

for.name: Cedric Richmond
for.what_they_did: Introduced the bill to expand USPS financial services.

against.name: House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform
against.what_they_did: Referred to committee but took no further action on the bill.

sides.party_line_note: Sponsor and all original cosponsors were Democrats.

industries.note: Would have competed with these businesses by offering cheaper financial alternatives through USPS.
Might lose customers but could also partner with USPS to deliver services.
New revenue source and expanded services at a time of declining mail volume.
